title: Trace Chizarira's hidden gorges
description: Explore a remote escarpment park of deep gorges, springs and broad Zambezi Valley views. Access finishes with a dirt-road climb to headquarters; arrive self-sufficient with food, water, first aid and camping equipment if staying overnight.

title: Watch waterbirds gather on Kazuma Pan
description: Drive the open grassland of one of Zimbabwe's least-visited parks when rain fills its pans and draws large numbers of waterbirds. Entry arrangements and road conditions should be confirmed with ZimParks because the border-area park is remote.

title: Descend to Chinhoyi's blue Sleeping Pool
description: Walk carefully into Zimbabwe's extensive limestone-and-dolomite cave system to see the clear blue Sleeping Pool. The rocks can be slippery, and the caves carry both documented local history and continuing spiritual significance.

title: Birdwatch and boat at quiet Umzingwane
description: Spend a low-key day birdwatching or boating at a recreational park about 38 kilometres southeast of Bulawayo. Bring supplies and keep well back from the shore where crocodiles and hippos are present.

title: Walk the Potholes route in Umfurudzi
description: Arrange a scenic walk to the Potholes within Umfurudzi's established tourism zone. The current park plan permits hiking, walking safaris, swimming and picnicking there; confirm access and guiding with management before travel.

title: Swim below the veils of Kundalila Falls
description: Follow the Kaombe River to a 70-metre fall surrounded by a natural botanical garden. Visitors can view the Luangwa Valley from above or swim in the deep pool below; check water conditions before entering.

title: Camp beside remote Lumangwe Falls
description: Detour nine kilometres from the Kawambwa-Mporokoso road to a broad waterfall that sustains a pocket of rainforest. Simple visitor facilities allow camping, but the remote location calls for supplies and current road advice.

title: Find the three cascades of Kabweluma
description: Walk to three successive cascades five kilometres downstream from Lumangwe, with a wooded ravine and rock paintings nearby. Kabweluma is a revered local shrine, so follow local guidance and behave respectfully.

title: Walk behind the water at Chisimba Falls
description: Explore trails and viewpoints around three linked falls on the Luombe River, including a path behind the water into a sacred cave. Respect the site's Bemba spiritual rules and use care on wet ground.

title: Follow the long cascade sequence at Chipoma
description: Trace a 500-metre sequence of rapids and small falls on the Chimanabwe River, with a total drop of about 40 metres. The official tourism page says the falls reach their maximum flow in January and gives the turnoff south of Chinsali.

title: Hike to the waterfalls above Gurué
description: Reach clear cascades near the Licungo headwaters by 4x4 approach or on foot, then continue on ecological trails through the Namuli landscape. Arrange local guidance and check track conditions before leaving Gurué.

title: Walk from tea country into the Namuli Mountains
description: Explore the highland scenery around Mount Namuli, where mountain slopes meet tea and coffee country. The national tourism authority presents the range for nature and agricultural tourism; arrange a guide and current route advice locally.

title: Climb to Chinhamapere's sacred rock art
description: Hike with a local guide to rock paintings at Chinhamapere, a place the national tourism authority describes as sacred to nearby communities. Ask permission locally, follow cultural guidance and confirm trail conditions before climbing.

title: Snorkel Inhaca's biologically rich coast
description: Cross Maputo Bay to snorkel around an island recognised for biological importance and diverse marine life, including coral, turtles and marine mammals. Use a local operator and check tides, weather and protected-area rules.

title: Track Coquerel's sifakas in Ankarafantsika
description: Walk a signed circuit through dry forest habitat for Coquerel's sifaka and other endemic wildlife. Madagascar National Parks says the park is accessible throughout the year via the RN4; use its local guiding system.

title: Walk the Simpona circuit for silky sifakas
description: Hike between Camp Mantella and Camp Marojejya through the transition from lowland to mid-altitude forest, watching for the rare silky sifaka. The drier window from August to mid-November is the park's preferred general visiting period.

title: Follow Baie de Baly's Bemosary beach circuit
description: Join a park agent or local village guide for a six-hour beach-and-forest circuit in Baie de Baly. The route is designed for spotting day lemurs, chameleons, snakes and forest birds.

title: Climb Zahamena's Bemoara forest circuit
description: Take the steep three-hour Bemoara route through eastern rainforest habitat for indri, ruffed lemurs, orchids and giant ferns. Confirm local access and guiding before travelling to this rarely visited park.

title: Hike with community guides to Dindéfélo Falls
description: Walk through a community-managed reserve to the Dindéfélo cascade while supporting trained local guides and conservation. Current reporting confirms regular visitors and a locally collected entry fee; arrange the visit through the reserve.

title: Explore Palmarin's community reserve
description: Book a locally managed nature visit in Palmarin at the edge of the Saloum landscape. The reserve's deputy conservator describes tourism revenue as part of its community conservation model and confirms year-round visitation.

title: Join an ecoguide in Guembeul reserve
description: Visit this Ramsar wetland with a community ecoguide to watch birds and learn how the reserve breeds threatened antelope for transfer to other protected areas. The reserve receives visitors year-round and has a small welcome area for local crafts.

title: Walk the bird-rich forests of Dzalanyama
description: Take a shaded forest walk in Dzalanyama, one of the reserves highlighted by Malawi's tourism department for hiking and strong birdlife. Confirm a suitable route and local access before departure.

title: Hike beneath Ntchisi's shady canopy
description: Walk in the cool forest of Ntchisi, which Malawi's official tourism site recommends for pleasant trails and birdwatching. Ask locally about current trail conditions and whether guidance is needed.

title: Meet Malawi's deep past at Karonga Museum
description: See dinosaur fossils alongside early-human and prehistoric material at the Culture and Museum Centre Karonga. The government tourism page identifies the museum as a partnership with Malawi's Department of Museums and Monuments.

title: Walk the gentle Coq Du Bois Loop
place: Bras d'Eau Coq Du Bois Loop
description: Follow a gentle forest loop past an old orchard in Mauritius's quieter Bras d'Eau National Park. Stop at the visitor centre for current trail information and watch for endemic birds around the woods and Mare Sarcelle.

title: See shipwreck relics at Mahébourg Museum
description: Explore an 18th-century mansion containing old maps, weapons, a dodo skeleton and material recovered from shipwrecks and naval battles. The national heritage building also has extensive gardens and a reconstructed colonial village.

title: Trace Dutch and French history at Frederik Hendrik
place: Frederik Hendrik Museum and fort ruins
description: Visit a small museum and the ruins of a Dutch fort at Vieux Grand Port. Archaeological finds and surviving spaces including a prison, bakery and blacksmith workshop span roughly four centuries of island history.

title: Take the short forest path to Asenema Falls
description: Walk five minutes from the road on a marked rainforest trail to a small waterfall outside Akropong. Flow is strongest in the rainy season from April to October, and the approach has broad views over the Akuapem Hills.

title: Hike the demanding path to Nchiraa Falls
description: Take a challenging rural hike to Nchiraa Waterfalls about 30 kilometres north of Wenchi. Ask locally about the route and consider combining the trip with the nearby Wurobo ancestral caves.

title: Watch Mona monkeys at Duasidan
description: Visit a small sanctuary about 10 kilometres southwest of Dormaa Ahenkro to see Mona monkeys moving through bamboo habitat. Confirm current opening and local guiding arrangements before making the detour.
